name: Korg NAUTILUS Combination
description: Korg NAUTILUS: the timbres, effects and controllers of a combination by SysEx parameter change, read back from the current combination.

sources.title: NAUTILUS MIDI Implementation: Combination, object version 4

sources.title: NAUTILUS MIDI Implementation: SysExDumps/Effect.txt
sources.notes: SysExDumps/Effect.txt (sha256 96bbc829519557ad68f4f5646fe3f7da7b3d196b721289091efd2637b988bc9d) in NAUTILUS_MIDIimp.zip, read by readEffectTables into tools/profiles/korg/tables/; shared by the instrument's profiles.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/korg/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/korg/synths/, not this file.

Every row of SysExDumps/CombiAndSongTimbreSet.txt with a parameter id is a parameter, named by its group and its name as printed, and sent by Parameter Change (function 43): F0 42 3g 00 01 5D 43 TYP SOC SUB PID IDX and the value as 21 bits, two's complement, high byte first (*4). Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

The rows of Scene Common with TYP 5… go by Scene Parameter Change (function 6D), the same message as Parameter Change under another code: Scene Common takes the KRONOS KARMA Common's ids for its own settings (Tempo PID 0, Latch Switch PID 3, the arpeggiator's switch PID 4), and KARMA Common goes by KARMA Parameter Change. The table prints no message per row. Per group, the rows whose ids Parameter Change also takes for another row, and so cannot go by it: Scene Common, 0 of 31. A group with such rows cannot go by Parameter Change; one with none goes by 6D on the reason given alone. A reading, not tried on an instrument.

The rows of Scene… go by Arp/Drum Track Parameter Change (function 6E), the same message as Parameter Change under another code: the scenes' arpeggiator and drum track settings, by the message's name. The table prints no message per row. Per group, the rows whose ids Parameter Change also takes for another row, and so cannot go by it: Scene 1, 0 of 38; Scene 2, 0 of 38; Scene 3, 0 of 38; Scene 4, 0 of 38; Scene Common, 0 of 8. A group with such rows cannot go by Parameter Change; one with none goes by 6E on the reason given alone. A reading, not tried on an instrument.

The rows of Step Seq.… go by Arp/Drum Track Parameter Change (function 6E), the same message as Parameter Change under another code: the drum track's step sequencers, by the message's name. The table prints no message per row. Per group, the rows whose ids Parameter Change also takes for another row, and so cannot go by it: Step Seq. A, 0 of 836; Step Seq. B, 0 of 836; Step Seq. C, 0 of 836; Step Seq. D, 0 of 836. A group with such rows cannot go by Parameter Change; one with none goes by 6E on the reason given alone. A reading, not tried on an instrument.

A combination: its sixteen timbres, its effects and controllers. The programs its timbres play are edited in Program mode (korg-nautilus). The NAUTILUS takes combination parameters in Combination mode ("Which parameters are currently available for editing depends on the instrument's mode").

The effects' own parameters: 1072 for the 16 effect slots, a parameter per pid of Effect.txt (`Insert Effect1 Parameter 5`), sent by Parameter Change as TYP 23 with the slot in SOC and the pid in PID. The table's effect switch goes out as that address with pid 0 (`23 0 0 0 0`, `* -> bypass`), and pid 0 is Bypass in every type, which the builder checks: TYP 23 is read as the effects' own parameters, a reading, not tried on an instrument. A pid means what the slot's effect type makes it (its description gives some), so its range is the widest any type gives it, and it is not read back: each type lays the slot's bytes out its own way. Effect Type is a choice of the 198 types its range 0~197 reaches.

A range whose first value is the larger (9D~63) is two's complement over its bytes, -99~+99. A choice is a row naming both of two values. The value column is 19 characters wide; a name it cuts short keeps its cut, with an ellipsis. Other value names are in each parameter's description.
3 rows with an id print a fixed value (`10(fixed)`, `00(fixed)`: Insert Effect11 Chain To; Insert Effect12 Chain Switch; Insert Effect12 Chain To; …) and are not settings.

Left out: 23 settings (Insert Effect1 Chain Switch; Insert Effect1 Chain To; Insert Effect2 Chain Switch; Insert Effect2 Chain To; Insert Effect3 Chain Switch; Insert Effect3 Chain To; …): shares its parameter id with Chain To (`* Chain To`), and the archive does not say which value of it turns the chain off.
Left out: 1 setting (Scene Common Drum Input Channel): no range printed (data(hex) is blank).
Left out: 4 settings (Step Seq. A (offset 1386); Step Seq. B (offset 1650); Step Seq. C (offset 1914); Step Seq. D (offset 2178)): printed with a group and no name.

Left out: 528 settings (Timbre1 Knob1 Assign; Timbre1 Knob2 Assign; Timbre1 Knob3 Assign; Timbre1 Knob4 Assign; Timbre1 Knob5 Assign; Timbre1 Knob6 Assign; …): its parameter change takes SUB from the value (`SUB = (Assign >> 7) & 0x01, Value = Assign & 0x7f`), which one message template cannot.

Pull: Current Object Dump Request (function 74) for object 01, the combination, answered by a Current Object Dump (function 75) carrying object version 4 and 5640 bytes in Korg's 8-in-7 packing (*3: 6446 bytes). 5967 parameters are read back at their rows' offsets and bits. A dump of any other length does not match.

Byte order: a value over whole bytes is read low byte first, and a field that runs on into the next byte has its low bits in the earlier one. The tables fill each byte from bit 0 upward (every effect's Bypass is bit 0 of its first byte, Wet/Dry bits 7~1 beside it), and a field crossing a byte continues upward in the next (an EXi engine's [LFO1] Start Phase at bits 7~5, then 3~0): the layout of a little-endian structure. A reading, not tried on an instrument.
The exclusive header carries the global MIDI channel as 3g; the profile's deviceId variable is that byte, 30H for channel 1.

Identity: the Device Inquiry reply (NAUTILUS_MIDI_MIDI_Implentaion.txt) is printed F0 7E 0g 06 02 42 00 01 5D 00 mm 00 vv ww xx 00 F7, 17 bytes where the universal reply has 15. Its 7th to 10th bytes, 00 01 5D 00, are checked as printed, where the universal reply puts the family and member code; its 11th byte, mm, is one per model and is not checked: NAUTILUS 61Keys 05H, NAUTILUS 73Keys 0EH, NAUTILUS 88Keys 17H.

Preset recall: Bank Select MSB and LSB, then Program Change, for the 14 banks the implementation's receive table gives in Combination mode when Global's Bank Map is KORG (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N). With Bank Map GM(2) the MSBs differ, and this recall does not apply.
